item.title: Q&amp;A: How Expandido Arts Collective is reimagining Medea
item.description: Originally written in Portuguese as Mata Teu Pai, Passô’s play reimagines the myth of Medea through a contemporary feminist lens.

item.title: Four theatre leaders on the highs and lows of venue management
item.description: "I’m very concerned that federal [funding] for cultural infrastructure in this country has completely disappeared," says Heather Redfern.

item.title: Tarragon reveals premiere-packed 55th anniversary season
item.description: Tarragon Theatre’s 2026-27 season features world premieres by Anahita Dehbonehie, Katherine Gauthier, Ho Ka Kei (Jeff Ho), and Luke Reece.

item.title: Review: Tarragon’s 'Queen Maeve' packs an emotional wallop
item.description: Coulter manages to appear one moment as if she’d blow away in a faint breeze, another as though she’d cleave you in twain with a broadsword.

item.title: Review: Shifting Ground’s 'The Drowsy Chaperone' is no snore
item.description: Infused with infectious energy, 'The Drowsy Chaperone' is a harmony of well-crafted design elements and vivacious performances.

item.title: Review: 'A Mirror' is a dystopian, metatheatrical marvel
item.description: Over the course of two tense hours, ARC's 'A Mirror' scrutinizes censorship, the responsibility of art, and the cost of insurgency.

item.title: 'Rise, Red River' is a multilingual vision of Indigenous survivance
item.description: “A big part of what I consider this writing to be is an honoring of ancestors that I will never meet in person,” says Beagan.

item.title: Canadian Stage 2026-27 season includes Cabaret
item.description: Casting highlights include Sara Farb and Allan Louis in Cabaret and Paul Gross returning to Canadian Stage in Creditors.

item.title: 2026 TOsketchfest paid tribue to sketch comedy's possibilities
item.description: Sketch is a genre that defies genre. And luckily, in Toronto, there are so many artists that constantly redefine it.

item.title: Review: Eros overpowers logos in Icarus Theatre’s 'Julie'
item.description: Director Jordan Laffrenier focuses on atmosphere, delivering a heightened production that takes inspiration from 1990s erotic thrillers.

item.title: Jasmine Case has plenty to chew on in 'Clyde's' at Canadian Stage
item.description: “She’s a mother who has a child that deals with epilepsy,” says Case, “and I grew up with epilepsy. I had a grand mal seizure as a kid."

item.title: Review: 'Anywhere' simmers with tension at the Assembly Theatre
item.description: The back and forth between actors Kaitlin Race and Anne van Leeuwen, who swap roles from night to night, is exhilarating to watch.

item.title: The Grand’s 'Importance of Being Earnest' focuses on queerness
item.description: "The entire physical production has been enacted to get people to try to keep their ears and their eyes open," says director Alistair Newton.

item.title: Review: 'A Cabaret of Legends' is a revisionist tribute show
item.description: 'A Cabaret of Legends' features Tymisha Harris' renditions of Nina Simone, Aretha Franklin, and Patti LaBelle to name a few.

item.title: Review: Tomson Highway’s 'Rose' makes long-awaited premiere
item.description: 'Rose' is, in many ways, a story oriented around grief — particularly queer and lesbian grief for Indigenous women.
